title: Omnigent ships as a paid Databricks-managed agent-orchestration tier by Q2 2027
body: Databricks introduced Omnigent on June 13 as an Apache 2.0, alpha-stage meta-harness: a layer that sits above individual coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi) and agent SDKs (OpenAI Agents, Claude Agents SDK) so a developer drives several of them through one interface, with stateful policies, cost budgets, permissions and OS-level sandboxing enforced at the meta-harness layer, plus shareable live sessions and cloud execution on Modal and Daytona sandboxes. Crucially it was published as a standalone OSS project on GitHub (omnigent-ai/omnigent) rather than a Databricks-only feature, and it landed alongside the Data + AI Summit. The business read is that this is the opening move of an open-core go-to-market, not a charity release: the same playbook that built Databricks around open-source Spark and Delta. Giving away the orchestration and policy layer seeds adoption and makes Omnigent the default control point a team standardizes on; the durable revenue is the managed runtime, hosted execution, identity and governance, and enterprise support that sit underneath it. The forward thesis is that Databricks converts that adoption into a commercial, first-party managed offering on its own platform. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q2 2027 Databricks publicly offers a priced, Databricks-hosted Omnigent-based agent-orchestration product - a managed runtime, hosted/cloud execution, or enterprise governance tier that is generally available or in a paid preview - announced by Databricks (blog, pricing page, Data + AI Summit / keynote, or a Databricks press release) and tied to Databricks-billed consumption (DBUs) or a subscription. What does NOT count: the OSS repo staying free with no paid Databricks-hosted tier; a third party (not Databricks) commercializing it; a free managed preview with no path to billing; an unpriced 'coming soon' teaser; or a generic Databricks agent product that does not build on or productize Omnigent. The counter-risk is that Databricks keeps Omnigent purely community OSS and monetizes agents only through its existing Mosaic AI / Agent Bricks surface, leaving Omnigent itself unmonetized through mid-2027.

reasoning.because: Databricks open-sourced the Omnigent meta-harness (Apache 2.0) June 13 as a standalone OSS project
reasoning.given: Open-core is the proven data-platform GTM: free the layer, charge for managed runtime + governance
reasoning.so_that: Databricks ships a paid managed Omnigent tier with hosted execution, cost/permission governance and an SLA
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; a priced Databricks-hosted Omnigent product, GA or paid preview
reasoning.plain_language: Databricks gave away the free tool that runs many AI agents, so it will likely sell a paid hosted version companies pay for.

summary: Databricks open-sourced Omnigent, a meta-harness over multiple coding agents, as a standalone Apache 2.0 project alongside its Data + AI Summit. That mirrors the open-core playbook behind Spark and Delta, so by Q2 2027 Databricks should offer a priced, hosted Omnigent orchestration tier.
